text_zh: 菩提達磨大師略辨大乘入道四行觀 No. 1217-A 弟子　曇琳　序
text_en: Great Master Bodhidharma’s Brief Explanation of the Four Practices for Entering the Mahayana Path No. 1217-A 弟子　曇琳　序 法師者，西域南天竺國人，是婆羅門國王第三之

text_zh: 法師者，西域南天竺國人，是婆羅門國王第三之 子也。神慧疎朗，聞皆曉悟。志存摩訶衍道，故捨素 隨緇，紹隆聖種。冥心虗寂，通鑒世事，內外俱明，德 超世表。悲悔邊隅正教陵替，遂能遠涉山海，遊化 漢魏。亡心之士，莫不歸信；存見之流，乃生譏謗。于 時唯有道育、惠可此二沙門，年雖後生，俊志高遠。 幸逢法師，事之數載。虔恭𧫎啟，善蒙師意。法師感 其精誠，誨以真道，令如是安心，如是發行，如是順 物，如是方便。此是大乘安心之法，令無錯謬。如是 安心者，壁觀。如是發行者，四行。如是順物者，防護 譏嫌。如是方便者，遣其不著。此略序所由云爾。
text_en: 子也。神慧疎朗，聞皆曉悟。志存摩訶衍道，故捨素 隨緇，紹隆聖種。冥心虗寂，通鑒世事，內外俱明，德 超世表。悲悔邊隅正教陵替，遂能遠涉山海，遊化 漢魏。亡心之士，莫不歸信；存見之流，乃生譏謗。于 時唯有道育、惠可此二沙門，年雖後生，俊志高遠。 幸逢法師，事之數載。虔恭 𧫎 啟，善蒙師意。法師感 其精誠，誨以真道，令如是安心，如是發行，如是順 物，如是方便。此是大乘安心之法，令無錯謬。如是 安心者，壁觀。如是發行者，四行。如是順物者，防護 譏嫌。如是方便者，遣其不著。此略序所由云爾。
Great Master Bodhidharma’s Four Practices No. 1217 There are many routes to enter the Way, but when reduced to essentials they do not go beyond two kinds: entry by principle and entry by practice.

text_zh: 夫入道多途，要而言之，不出二種：一是理入，二是行 入。理入者，謂藉教悟宗，深信含生同一真性，但為客 塵妄想所覆，不能顯了。若也捨妄歸真，凝住壁觀，無 自無他，凡聖等一，堅住不移，更不隨文教，此即與理 冥符，無有分別，寂然無為，名之理入。行入謂四行，其 餘諸行，悉入此中。何等四耶？一報冤行，二隨緣行，三 無所求行，四稱法行。云何？
text_en: Entry by principle means relying on the teaching to awaken to the fundamental point, and firmly believing that all sentient beings share the same true nature. It is only because this true nature is covered over by adventitious defilements and false thoughts that it cannot appear clearly. If one abandons the false and returns to the true, settles firmly in wall-contemplation, without self and without other, seeing ordinary beings and sages as equally one, abiding steadfastly without wavering, and no longer following written formulations, then one comes into silent accord with principle, free of discrimination, quiet and without contrived action. This is called entry by principle. Entry by practice means the four practices; all other practices are included within them. What are the four? First, the practice of accepting karmic retribution. Second, the practice of adapting to conditions. Third, the practice of seeking nothing. Fourth, the practice of acting in accord with the Dharma. How is this so?
“The practice of accepting karmic retribution” means this: when someone training in the Way undergoes suffering, they should reflect: “For countless ages in the past,

text_zh: 報冤行，謂修道行人，若受苦時，當自念言：「我往昔無 數劫中，棄本從末，流浪諸有，多起冤憎，違害無限。今 雖無犯，是我宿殃，惡業果熟，非天非人所能見與，甘 心甘受，都無冤訴。經云：『逢苦不憂。何以故？識達故。』」此 心生時，與理相應，體冤進道，故說言報冤行。
text_en: I turned away from what is fundamental and followed what is secondary. I wandered through the many states of existence, again and again giving rise to resentment and hatred, causing harm without measure. So although I am not at fault now, what I now endure is the ripening of my past wrongs, the maturing fruit of harmful karma. This is not something that gods or human beings can see and assign. I should accept it willingly, with no resentment or complaint.” A scripture says: “When suffering is encountered, do not be distressed. Why? Because there is understanding.” When this frame of mind arises, it accords with principle. By taking up wrongs in this way, one advances on the Way. That is why it is called “the practice of accepting karmic retribution.”

Second is “the practice of adapting to conditions.” Sentient beings are without a fixed self, and they are carried along by karma as conditions act upon them. Suffering and pleasure are both received in this way, since they arise from

text_zh: 二、隨緣行者，眾生無我，並緣業所轉，苦樂齊受皆從 緣生，若得勝報榮譽等事，是我過去宿因所感今方 得之，緣盡還無，何喜之有？得失從緣心無增減，喜風 不動冥順於道，是故說言隨緣行。
text_en: conditions. If one comes to enjoy a favorable result—honor, prestige, or similar things—that is the effect of causes formed in the past, only now coming to fruition. When the conditions that support it are exhausted, it disappears again. So what is there to delight in? Gain and loss both depend on conditions, and the mind neither increases nor diminishes because of them. If the wind of joy does not stir it, one comes quietly into accord with the Way. For this reason, this is called “the practice of adapting to conditions.”
Third is “the practice of seeking nothing.” People in the world remain deluded for a long time. Everywhere they become attached and pursue what they desire. This is what is called seeking. The wise

text_zh: 三、無所求行者，世人長迷，處處貪著，名之為求。智者 悟真，理將俗反，安心無為，形隨運轉，萬有斯空，無所 願樂，功德黑暗，常相隨逐，三界久居，猶如火宅，有身 皆苦，誰得而安？了達此處，故捨諸有，止想無求。經曰： 「有求皆苦，無求即樂。」判知無求，真為道行，故言無所 求行。
text_en: awaken to what is true. They realize that principle runs counter to ordinary worldly ways. So they settle the mind in non-contrivance, and let the body move with the turn of conditions. In this way, all things are seen to be empty, with nothing to long for or take pleasure in. Favorable and dark conditions continually follow one another. To dwell for long in the three realms is like living in a burning house. As long as one has a body, there is suffering. Who can find peace in that? Once this is fully understood, one lets go of all modes of existence, brings thought to rest, and no longer seeks. The sutra says: “Where there is seeking, there is suffering; where there is no seeking, there is joy.” From this one can clearly know that non-seeking is truly practice of the Way. That is why it is called “the practice of seeking nothing.”
Fourth is “the practice of acting in accord with the Dharma.” Dharma here means the principle that one’s nature is pure. From that principle, all appearances are empty: free of

text_zh: 四稱法行者，性淨之理目之為法，此理眾相斯空，無 染無著、無此無彼。經曰：「法無眾生，離眾生垢故；法無 有我，離我垢故。」智者若能信解此理，應當稱法而行。 法體無慳，身命財行檀捨施，心無恡惜，脫解三空不 倚不著，但為去垢，稱化眾生而不取相，此為自行復 能利他，亦能莊嚴菩提之道。檀施既爾，餘五亦然。為 除妄想修行六度而無所行，是為稱法行。
text_en: defilement, free of attachment, with no this and no that. As the scripture says, “In the Dharma there are no sentient beings, because it is free from the defilement of sentient beings. In the Dharma there is no self, because it is free from the defilement of self.” If a wise person can trust and understand this principle, that person should practice in accord with the Dharma. The essence of the Dharma is without stinginess. So one gives body, life, and possessions in generosity, with a mind that does not hold back or cling. Free of fixation on the threefold emptiness, without dependence and without attachment, one acts only to remove defilement, working to guide sentient beings without grasping at appearances. This is practice for oneself, and it is also able to benefit others. It also adorns the path to awakening. What is true of giving is true of the other five perfections as well. In order to remove deluded thoughts, one cultivates the six perfections, yet without taking there to be anything that is being practiced. This is what is meant by “acting in accord with the Dharma.”

text_zh: 達磨大師四行觀終 No. 1217-B (附)達磨大師󳬴頌 梁武帝蕭衍
text_en: Great Master Bodhidharma’s Four Practices 終 No. 1217-B (附)達磨大師 󳬴 頌 梁 武帝蕭衍 楞伽山頂坐寶日， 中有金人披縷褐，

text_zh: 楞伽山頂坐寶日，　中有金人披縷褐， 形同大地體如空，　心如瑠璃色如雪。 匪磨匪瑩恒淨明，　披雲卷霧心且徹， 芬陀利花用嚴身，　隨緣髑物常次悅。 不有不無非去來，　多聞辨才無法說， 實哉空哉離生有，　大之小之眾緣絕。 剎那而登妙覺心，　躍鱗慧海起先哲， 理應法水永長流，　何期暫涌還蹔渴。 驪龍珠內落心燈，　白毫慧刃當鋒缼， 生途忽鳥慧眼閉，　禪河駐流法梁折。 無去無來無是非，　彼此形體心碎裂， 住烏去烏皆歸寂，　寂內何曾存哽咽。 用之執手以傳燈，　生死去來如電掣， 有能至誠心不疑，　劫火燃燈斯不滅。 一真之法盡可有，　未悟迷途茲是竭。
text_en: 形同大地體如空， 心如瑠璃色如雪。 匪磨匪瑩恒淨明， 披雲卷霧心且徹， 芬陀利花用嚴身， 隨緣髑物常 次悅。 不有不無非去來， 多聞辨才無法說， 實哉空哉離生有， 大之小之眾緣絕。 剎那而登妙覺心， 躍鱗慧海起先哲， 理應法水永長流， 何期暫涌還蹔渴。 驪龍珠內落心燈， 白毫慧刃當鋒缼， 生途忽 鳥慧眼閉， 禪河駐流法梁折。 無去無來無是非， 彼此形體心碎裂， 住 烏去烏皆歸寂， 寂內何曾存哽咽。 用之執手以傳燈， 生死去來如電掣， 有能至誠心不疑， 劫火燃燈斯不滅。 一真之法盡可有， 未悟迷途茲是竭。
